attempts.label: CRCNS:ac-4
attempts.entry_title: Rapid tuning shifts in human auditory cortex (Holdgraf et al. 2016)
attempts.summary: The paper's main neural effects of speech context hold up in this data: high-frequency activity rose for filtered speech heard after its clear version and became more coherent with the response to the clear sentence. The behavioural finding that context improves intelligibility could not be tested, as the listener data are not in the dataset. The encoding-model analyses rest on 9 well-modelled electrodes against the paper's 41, likely because the paper does not say how model scores and the ridge parameter were computed. On those electrodes, tuning moved towards that of clear speech, mostly on superior temporal gyrus, but the shift towards the modulations the filter kept did not reproduce.
attempts.description: Tests the ECoG findings of Holdgraf, de Heer, Pasley, Rieger, Crone, Lin, Knight and Theunissen (2016) on CRCNS data set ac-4, which holds the raw ECoG of seven patients listening to filtered, unfiltered and again filtered sentences, with the stimulus audio. It tests the selection of speech-responsive and spectrotemporally tuned electrodes, the HFB increase and the coherence change from BEFORE to AFTER, the eSTRF comparisons, and the connectivity and spectral analyses of the supplement. The behavioural control data are not in the data set.

outcomes.statement: 92 of the 468 electrodes (19.6%) responded to speech above baseline (Speech-R), generally centred on perisylvian regions.

outcomes.source: Results, HFB activity, paragraph 3; Supplementary Figure 3A

outcomes.notes: On the pink noise triplets of S07, S08 and S13, no AFTER minus BEFORE cluster reaches P < 0.05 over their 36 Speech-R electrodes (smallest P = 0.0895). outcomes.statement: Trial by trial, the time-varying HFB response in AFTER is more coherent with the MIDDLE response to the same sentence than the BEFORE response is, in both post-stimulus windows (0 to 1 s P = 0.000, 1 to 3 s P = 0.001), and not before the sound (P = 0.924).
outcomes.source: Results, Between-condition HFB coherence, paragraph 2; Figure 4a
outcomes.quote: The coherence between AFTER/MIDDLE was higher than the coherence between BEFORE/MIDDLE, indicating it was not only the mean amplitude, but also the time-varying activity that was changing from BEFORE to AFTER (permutation test
outcomes.notes: With NW = 4, on the 84 Speech-R electrodes on temporal or perisylvian cortex (set a), AFTER/MIDDLE minus BEFORE/MIDDLE coherence is +0.80 bits/s over 0 to 1 s (P = 0.0003) and +0.49 over 1 to 2.5 s (P = 0.0004); before the sound +0.31 (P = 0.14, one window). Windows assigned by centre give P = 0.0002 and 0.0003, and 0.82 before the sound. On all 251 temporal or perisylvian electrodes (set b) only 1 to 2.5 s differs (P = 0.0003; 0 to 1 s P = 0.44). With NW = 2, set (a) gives P = 0.0012 and 0.013, and the pre-stimulus window also differs (P = 0.013), against the paper's 0.924. Five of seven subjects have a positive mean difference (S02 -0.13, S03 -0.05 bits/s). Set (a) is adopted, as the Results compute it on speech-responsive electrodes and its 84 is close to the paper's 78. The integrated coherence is about 15 bits/s in both conditions (14.5 before the sound); how much of it is estimator bias is not measured here. Integrated from W = 10 Hz, the lowest frequency the NW = 4 tapers resolve apart from 0 Hz, set (a) still gives P = 0.013 and 0.0019 after the sound and 0.21 before it; NW = 2 integrated from 5 Hz gives 0.028 and 0.038, and 0.014 before the sound.
deviations: Speech-R carried into this claim is the reading z-score by non-event times, 0 to 2.5 s, MIDDLE trials (101 electrodes), the first reading within the paper's count in the claims file's order (see speech-r-count).

Assumed. The multitaper bandwidth is not given (claims, open detail 10, whose standard choice is MNE's multitaper default). MNE's default normalized half-bandwidth is 4 (mne.time_frequency.multitaper._compute_mt_params with bandwidth None), which for a 20-sample window gives seven tapers with concentration above 0.9; NW = 4 with seven tapers and a jackknife over tapers is used, integrated from 2.5 to 25 Hz. NW = 2 (three tapers), the first revision's choice, is shown as a variant.

Assumed. The claims file integrates from the lowest resolved frequency. 2.5 Hz (1 / 400 ms, the lowest nonzero frequency of the window) is used; integrating from the tapers' half-bandwidth W = NW / 0.4 s (10 Hz at NW = 4, 5 Hz at NW = 2) is shown as a variant.

A window belongs to a range of Figure 4 when it lies wholly inside it, so the -1 to 0 s range holds one window (-0.5 to -0.1 s), 0 to 1 s three and 1 to 2.5 s six; assignment by window centre is shown as a variant.

outcomes.statement: After subtracting each electrode's mean evoked response over all trials, coherence between AFTER and MIDDLE stays higher than between BEFORE and MIDDLE, significant in the 1 to 3 s window (P = 0.006) but not 0 to 1 s (P = 0.241), so the change is sentence-specific and not only a global gain.
outcomes.source: Results, Between-condition HFB coherence, paragraph 3; Figure 4b
outcomes.quote: After subtracting this global response in each electrode, a significant increase in coherence between the responses in the AFTER/MIDDLE conditions remained
outcomes.notes: With NW = 4, on set (a), 1 to 2.5 s gives AFTER/MIDDLE higher with the mean over all trials subtracted (+0.29 bits/s, P = 0.0068) and with the mean per condition (+0.42, P = 0.0001). 0 to 1 s is not significant with the mean over all trials subtracted (P = 0.17, as the paper's 0.241) and is with the mean per condition (P = 0.014). On set (b) the late window gives P = 0.015 and 0.0002. With NW = 2, set (a) gives P = 0.11 (mean over all trials) and 0.012 (per condition) for the late window, so with three tapers the claim holds under one subtraction only. outcomes.statement: 53 of 468 electrodes (11.3%) were well modelled by the eSTRF (STRF-R), generally on perisylvian temporal lobe.
outcomes.source: Results, eSTRF modelling, paragraph 2; Figure 5b
outcomes.quote: This yielded 53 of 468 total electrodes (11.3%
outcomes.notes: With leave-one-trial-out ridge on the MIDDLE trials, 9 electrodes are STRF-R under the bootstrap bound (a), 0 under the per-split percentiles (b, c); with samples to 400 ms after offset, 13, 1 and 1. The paper reports 53. Only about 19 electrodes have a mean held-out R2 above 0 at any ridge value; the STRF-R electrodes have mean R2 0.044 to 0.226. They come from S01 (4), S02 (1) and S04 (4); none from S03, S07, S08 or S13. Alignment check: refitting the MIDDLE eSTRF with the spectrogram read -0.5 to +0.5 s against the HFB, the best median R2 lies at -0.1 s in S01 and 0 s in S04, the subjects where models work, and the evoked HFB reaches half its rise 0.10 to 0.16 s after the spectrogram there. In S03, S07 and S13 no shift gives any Speech-R electrode a positive R2, and in S02 and S08 at most 3 do at any shift, so no single offset would raise the count. The median held-out R2 of Speech-R electrodes is below 0 in 6 of 7 subjects, while the paper's Figure 6b shows scores near or above 0 for nearly all electrodes. The audio of S02, S04, S07 and S13 is not silent before the sounds (spectrogram before onset 0.43 to 0.66 of that after) and S03's evoked HFB is weak (peak 0.22 z). Drift check: with the MIDDLE trials split by onset into halves and shifts searched from -1 to +1 s, the best shift is the same in both halves in S01, S02, S04 and S13 (-0.1, 0, 0, 0 s); it differs in S03 (-0.7 and 0 s), S07 (-0.7 and 0 s) and S08 (0 and -0.4 s), but there no shift in either half gives more than 4 Speech-R electrodes a positive R2 (S07 none) and the median R2 at the best shift is below 0. On the wider grid S07's best median R2 over all trials lies at -0.6 s, with no electrode above 0. No offset or drift found here raises the count.
deviations: The ridge parameter is the mode of the per-split best values over Speech-R electrodes and the three conditions, leaving out values at the top of the grid (1e8). Assumed. The Methods take the mode of the selected values, but 2751 of 11860 values sit at the top of any grid, where no alpha predicts the held-out trial better than the null model, so the plain mode is the grid edge; the claims file asks for a grid whose mode is not at an edge. Both this mode and the mode of each electrode's best alpha give 1e5.

Auditory spectrogram compression (cube root) and spectral sharpening (rectified difference with the next lower band, as in the NSL model of the Methods' ref. 3) are standard choices; the gammatone filters are applied in the frequency domain.

HFB band edges and filter orders are not given (claims, open detail 4); 21 log-spaced centres 70 to 140 Hz, each band 10% of its centre wide, 2nd-order Butterworth applied forwards and backwards, as a standard choice.
Inputs and outputs are z-scored with each fold's training statistics; R2 is the coefficient of determination on the held-out trial, as the criterion says.

outcomes.statement: The modulation transfer functions of the eSTRFs match the filter type of the stimuli they were fit on, in BEFORE (P = 0.001), AFTER (P = 0.003) and in the AFTER minus BEFORE shift (P = 0.001), so the tuning change emphasizes modulations kept in the degraded speech.
outcomes.source: Results, Shifts in eSTRF modulation related to speech intelligibility; Figure 8b
outcomes.quote: The MTF of each eSTRF matches its respective filter type ... (cluster-based permutation t-test across electrodes
outcomes.notes: On 9 electrodes, temporal minus spectral MTF has a significant positive cluster in the region the temporal filter keeps in BEFORE (centre 2.1 Hz and 0.30 cycles per band, P = 0.0078) and in AFTER (2.0 Hz, P = 0.043, both rules; 1.6 Hz, P = 0.031, cutoff rule only). Most significant clusters lie at 16 to 19 Hz (P = 0.0039 to 0.027), outside both regions. For the shift, the MTF of the difference has one significant cluster, at 15.3 Hz (P = 0.0039), outside the regions under both rules, and the difference of MTFs none. The criterion asks for an in-region cluster in each of BEFORE, AFTER and the shift; the shift, which carries the claim's conclusion, has none. With 9 electrodes the smallest possible P is 0.0039.
deviations: Every eSTRF claim rests on the 9 included electrodes found here (S01 4, S02 1, S04 4), against the paper's 41 (see strf-r-count and included-electrode-count).

The ridge parameter is the mode of the per-split best values over Speech-R electrodes and the three conditions, leaving out values at the top of the grid (1e8). Assumed. The Methods take the mode of the selected values, but 2751 of 11860 values sit at the top of any grid, where no alpha predicts the held-out trial better than the null model, so the plain mode is the grid edge; the claims file asks for a grid whose mode is not at an edge. Both this mode and the mode of each electrode's best alpha give 1e5.

Auditory spectrogram compression (cube root) and spectral sharpening (rectified difference with the next lower band, as in the NSL model of the Methods' ref. 3) are standard choices; the gammatone filters are applied in the frequency domain.

Assumed (from the criterion, and made concrete here). Two rules: (1) low and high modulation are below and above the median of the plane's absolute temporal (11.9 Hz) and spectral (0.234 cycles per band) modulations, measured at the cluster's mean position; (2) from the filter cutoffs (Methods, Filtered speech sound creation), temporal modulation at most 3 Hz and spectral modulation at most 0.5 cycles/kHz, converted at the mean band spacing to 0.11 cycles per band, a cluster being in region when more than half its bins are.
The cluster test runs on the half plane of non-negative spectral modulation, as the amplitude spectrum of a real eSTRF is symmetric.

outcomes.notes: Integrated from W (10 Hz at NW = 4, 5 Hz at NW = 2), the lowest frequency the tapers resolve apart from 0 Hz, which the claims file's standard choice names as the start of the integration, neither target region shows an increase from BEFORE to AFTER with the 9 included electrodes as seeds (frontal P = 0.46, +0.052 bits/s, 5 of 9 seeds positive; temporal P = 0.72 at NW = 4; 0.23 and 0.41 at NW = 2). Integrated from 2.5 Hz with NW = 4, coherence rises with frontal and premotor targets (+0.27 bits/s, 9 of 9 seeds positive, t = 3.96, P = 0.0039) and temporal targets (+0.25, 7 of 9, t = 2.64, P = 0.039); of the frontal increase, 0.22 bits/s lies in the bins below 10 Hz, whose tapers reach 0 Hz. From 2.5 Hz the temporal targets give P = 0.070 at NW = 2, and the 6 temporal seeds of the Supplementary Methods give P = 0.094 at either bandwidth. The paper has 39 seeds; with 6 seeds the smallest possible P is 0.031. The seed set is asked of a reader (questions/crcns-ac-4.yaml). The outcome was reproduced (from 2.5 Hz) in rounds 1 and 2 and changed after round 3.

Seeds are all included electrodes, as the criterion says; the Supplementary Methods' temporal seeds (included and on the temporal lobe) are run as a variant.

Assumed. The coherence is integrated from the tapers' half-bandwidth W (10 Hz at NW = 4), read as the claims file's lowest resolved frequency, since on 400 ms windows the bins below W reach 0 Hz; integrating from 2.5 Hz, as for fig4a-coherence-after-higher, is shown as a variant and reproduces the claim.

Frontal targets are every frontal-* and premotor-* label, including the inferior ones that the region column counts as perisylvian (90 electrodes); temporal targets the other temporal electrodes, good channels only.

outcomes.statement: The seed to target HFB amplitude coherence in AFTER is closer than in BEFORE to that obtained with unfiltered speech.
outcomes.source: Results, Connectivity analysis, paragraph 1; Supplementary Figure 6A
outcomes.quote: Moreover, the coherence in the AFTER condition was closer to that obtained with the unfiltered speech
outcomes.notes: Integrated from W, as for supp6a-connectivity-increase, AFTER is not closer to MIDDLE in either region with the 9 included seeds (mean |AFTER - MIDDLE| against |BEFORE - MIDDLE|, frontal 0.248 against 0.241, temporal 0.207 against 0.143 at NW = 4, 2 of 9 seeds closer for temporal targets; 0.285 against 0.232 and 0.223 against 0.185 at NW = 2), and MIDDLE has the lowest coherence of the three conditions (8.44 and 8.42 against 8.54 to 8.69 bits/s at NW = 4). Integrated from 2.5 Hz with NW = 4, AFTER is closer for frontal targets (0.54 against 0.82, 9 of 9 seeds) and temporal targets (0.93 against 1.17, 7 of 9); with 9 seeds at NW = 2 the temporal targets do not (0.204 against 0.182). The coherence choices of supp6a-connectivity-increase.

outcomes.statement: Phase-amplitude coupling between 3 to 8 Hz phase in frontal/premotor electrodes and HFB amplitude in the eSTRF electrodes does not change from BEFORE to AFTER.
outcomes.source: Results, Connectivity analysis, paragraph 2; Supplementary Figure 6B; Supplementary Methods, Theta Connectivity Phase-Amplitude Coupling Analysis
outcomes.quote: In this analysis, however, we did not find significant inter-region cross-frequency activity that was modulated by task condition
outcomes.notes: PAC of 3 to 8 Hz frontal/premotor phase with the HFB amplitude of the 9 included electrodes changes by 0.00057 from BEFORE to AFTER (t = 1.60, P = 0.14). Variants give P = 0.063 (4 to 8 Hz) and 0.52 (2 to 12 Hz). One included electrode is also a phase electrode and is left out of its own phase mean. With 9 electrodes the test has little power.
deviations: Every eSTRF claim rests on the 9 included electrodes found here (S01 4, S02 1, S04 4), against the paper's 41 (see strf-r-count and included-electrode-count).

outcomes.notes: With NW = 4, in 66 temporal Speech-R electrodes MIDDLE minus BEFORE has positive clusters at 7.3 to 8.7 Hz (P = 0.012) and 1.3 to 2.3 Hz (P = 0.037), overlapping both theta ranges; no AFTER minus BEFORE cluster reaches P < 0.05 (smallest 0.095); in 19 frontal/premotor Speech-R electrodes no cluster of either test reaches P < 0.05 (smallest 0.081). Mean 3 to 8 Hz NMI in temporal electrodes 0.139 BEFORE, 0.154 MIDDLE, 0.141 AFTER bits. The temporal cluster lies at the upper edge of 3 to 8 Hz. With NW = 3 the outcome is not reproduced: no temporal MIDDLE minus BEFORE cluster reaches P < 0.05 (smallest 1.7 to 2.3 Hz, P = 0.093), and frontal MIDDLE exceeds BEFORE from 6.7 to 8.3 Hz (P = 0.0012). The paper has 72 temporal electrodes.

Signal and envelope resampled to 100 Hz; multitaper with MNE's default half-bandwidth NW = 4 (seven tapers), as for Figure 4 (claims, open detail 10), with a jackknife; NW = 3 (five tapers), the first revision's choice, as a variant, which gives the opposite outcome. 1 to 30 Hz tested, Gabor wavelets of 7 cycles for the envelope, a standard choice.

outcomes.statement: Power in the HFB range rises in AFTER against BEFORE in frontal (p = 0.001, n = 75) and temporal (p = 0.002, n = 217) electrodes, and power below 25 Hz falls in frontal electrodes (p = 0.001).
outcomes.source: Supplementary Figure 4B legend
outcomes.quote: Power in the high-frequency broadband (HFB) range significantly increased in ... the AFTER condition in both frontal and temporal electrodes (frontal, p=.001, n=75; ... temporal, p=.002, n=217). There was also a decrease in frequencies below 25 Hz in ... frontal electrodes (p=.001, n=75)
outcomes.notes: AFTER minus BEFORE power has a positive cluster over the HFB range in frontal/premotor electrodes (26 to 200 Hz, P = 0.0001, n = 90) and in temporal electrodes (51 to 200 Hz, P = 0.0005, n = 192), and a negative cluster in frontal electrodes from 4.2 to 19.4 Hz (P = 0.0001). Mean change 70 to 150 Hz, 0.23 dB frontal and 0.16 dB temporal; below 25 Hz, -0.33 dB frontal. Power after the stimulus without a baseline gives the same three effects: frontal 19 to 200 Hz (P = 0.0006), temporal 25 to 200 Hz (P = 0.0002), frontal decrease 3.9 to 6.7 Hz (P = 0.034).
deviations: Wavelets from 3 Hz, not the claims file's standard 1 Hz, as the kept epochs (-1 to 3.5 s) are too short for 5 cycles below about 3 Hz; post-stimulus 0 to 2.5 s, dB against -800 to -100 ms. Below about 10 Hz the wavelets reach the epoch start from the baseline, so post-stimulus power without a baseline is also tested.
Electrode groups from the channels.tsv labels (frontal-* and premotor-*, 90; temporal, 192) against the paper's 75 and 217.

findings.statement: The behavioural control data (three groups of 5, 9 and 15 listeners) behind Figure 2b and Supplementary Figures 1 and 5A are not in the data set, and the paper names no other place for them. Six of the paper's claims cannot be tested.

The data set holds 416 channels (377 marked good) for its 7 subjects, at most 64 per subject, while the paper reports grids of 48, 64, 68, 68, 62, 110 and 104 channels and 468 electrodes kept. The data set does not say which channels were left out or why.
The subjects are named S01, S02, S03, S04, S07, S08 and S13, the paper's S1 to S7, with no mapping between them, so per-subject results cannot be compared with the paper's figures.

channels.tsv gives the unit as milliV and the header a resolution of 0.1, but the stored float32 values have a median absolute value of about 315 in S01 and 1.7e8 to 6.2e8 in the other six subjects, so the scale is neither millivolts nor the same across subjects.

The data set's explore_data notebook and its per-subject copies say the audio files are not available for privacy reasons, and the README says subject folders are named like ir-07; the zip holds a stimulus track per subject (stimuli/<subject>_audio.wav) and folders named sub-S01. The audio tracks are on the recording's clock (the mean audio amplitude rises 2.7 to 211 times at the event onsets in every subject), but S07's track is 1015 s for a 989 s recording, and S13's is at 20 kHz against 16 kHz in the others; neither is documented.

The events tables of S01, S03, S04 and S07 hold spans with trial_type 'bad' (1 to 12 per subject) that events.json does not describe, and 22 sounds overlap them; the paper does not mention them. They were kept here.

One triplet in S02 and one in S03 lack a sound (46 of 47 and 38 of 39 complete), and S01 to S04 each have six unfiltered sentences outside any triplet (trial_num -1), which the data set does not explain.

The stimulus tracks of S02, S04, S07 and S13 are not silent before the sound onsets: the auditory spectrogram from 0.45 s to the onset is 0.43 to 0.66 of that in the first 0.5 s of the sound, against 0.02 to 0.14 in S01, S03 and S08. The data set does not say whether the tracks hold background noise or other sound, which enters any model of the neural response on the audio.

disagreements.reason: 3 of 12 readings fall inside 92 +/- 9.2 (96, 99, 101), and all three use the non-event z-score. The electrode total is 377 good of 416, against 468 +/- 46.8, so the fraction is 26.8% against 19.6%. The claims file lists the total of 468 +/- 46.8 as an expected value, while the criterion says the total is only reported; the data set's grids differ from the paper's, so the total cannot match.

n = 9: the AFTER minus BEFORE shift has no in-region cluster under either reading (shift_a's only significant cluster is out of region; shift_b has no cluster below 0.69). BEFORE (P = 0.0078) and AFTER (P = 0.043) pass only on a crude centroid rule, and most significant clusters lie outside the expected region. The filter region is judged against the grid median, while the filter cutoffs are 3 Hz and 0.5 cycles/kHz and the spectral axis is in cycles per band; the shift test fails either way.

Frontal P = 0.0312, temporal P = 0.094, from 6 seeds; with 6 seeds the smallest P the test can give is 0.031. Seeds are restricted to included electrodes on the temporal lobe (6), while the criterion says the included electrodes (9). The notebook's choice follows the Supplementary Methods, so here the claims file misreads the paper; its explanation of 39 vs 41 seeds is also unsupported. The notebook does not state the deviation. Could also move with the multitaper bandwidth (NW = 4).

paper_notes.statement: Question for the paper's authors. How was HFB z-scored to select Speech-R electrodes? With each trial's own -800 to -100 ms baseline or a pooled baseline, 131 to 185 electrodes pass here; with the whole series z-scored by its non-event times (ecogtools zscore_by_non_events) 96 to 104, near the paper's 92. This attempt assumed the latter.

Question for the paper's authors. How were the ridge parameter's mode and the STRF-R bound computed? Over Speech-R electrodes, a quarter of the per-split best values sit at the top of any grid, so the mode of all values is the grid edge; this attempt took the mode below the edge (1e5). With the held-out trial's coefficient of determination, only 9 electrodes pass the bound (the paper has 53). Was R2 computed per held-out trial, over a block of trials, or as a squared correlation? Figure 6b plots mean model scores near or above 0 for nearly all electrodes (most non-included ones near 0.07), while the held-out coefficient of determination here is below 0 for most electrodes, which suggests a different score.

Question for the paper's authors. What multitaper bandwidth was used for the 400 ms coherence windows of Figure 4 and Supplementary Figure 6A, and for the speech envelope coherence of Supplementary Figure 7, and over which frequencies was the coherence integrated? This attempt used MNE's default half-bandwidth (NW = 4, seven tapers), 2.5 to 25 Hz. With NW = 2 for Figure 4 and Supplementary Figure 6A, or NW = 3 for Supplementary Figure 7, fig4b holds under one subtraction only, the temporal targets of Supplementary Figure 6A are not significant (P = 0.070), and the temporal theta effect of Supplementary Figure 7 is not found.

Question for the paper's authors. On what scale is the RMS of Figure 9c (axis about 3.6 to 5.0) and the mean increase of 0.12? With standardized eSTRFs applied to z-scored spectrograms the RMS is about 105 here; the relative increase is 0.12 to 0.13.

entries.name: holdgraf-2016
entries.title: Rapid tuning shifts in human auditory cortex (Holdgraf et al. 2016)
entries.description: Tests the ECoG findings of Holdgraf, de Heer, Pasley, Rieger, Crone, Lin, Knight and Theunissen (2016) on CRCNS data set ac-4, which holds the raw ECoG of seven patients listening to filtered, unfiltered and again filtered sentences, with the stimulus audio. It tests the selection of speech-responsive and spectrotemporally tuned electrodes, the HFB increase and the coherence change from BEFORE to AFTER, the eSTRF comparisons, and the connectivity and spectral analyses of the supplement. The behavioural control data are not in the data set.
